evidence.historical_decision: Argentine Republic is not a separate sovereign state from Argentina. Article 35 of the Argentine Constitution declares Provincias Unidas del Río de la Plata, República Argentina and Confederación Argentina to be official names used indistinctly for the government and territory, with Nación Argentina used in legislation. Argentina's official denomination history further records that on 8 October 1860 President Santiago Derqui standardized República Argentina for administrative acts. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento's 1868-1874 presidency therefore belongs to the same continuous Argentina polity already used for later presidents; the duplicate Argentine Republic row is a formal-name identity split rather than a historical-state boundary.
evidence.naming_rule: Do not invent a bounded temporal official_name designation for Argentine Republic. República Argentina remains a current constitutional official name, while ATLAS polity_designations currently model closed temporal phases and an all-null end boundary means unresolved rather than ongoing. Preserve the formal-name fact in correction evidence and, after exhaustive orphan verification, in the polity retirement ledger; keep Argentina as the canonical survivor.

after.reviewed_notes: Domingo Faustino Sarmiento served as President from 12 October 1868 to 12 October 1874. Article 35 of the Argentine Constitution treats República Argentina as an official name of the same government and territory, not a separate polity. ATLAS therefore binds this presidency to the canonical Argentina identity while preserving the formal-name evidence separately from polity identity.
